sermon.title: Sodom’s Judgment
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 3 that in the midst of God’s judgments there are promises for those who repent: God is married to His people, gives shepherds who feed with knowledge, increases the righteous, and gathers the Gentiles to Zion, the church. He ends with hope for America and the call to bow to Jesus now.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “John 10:1” for “I am the good shepherd,” which is John 10:11; the words are kept as spoken. He says “Jeremiah is prophesying in 2 Corinthians 11:2,” where the quoted text is 2 Corinthians 11:2. “Bell” in the captions is corrected to “Baal,” and several caption slips were corrected (“chase” to “chaste,” “predition” to “perdition,” “writing” to “riding,” “prodal” to “prodigal,” “council” to “counsel”). The attendance and youth statistics are given as spoken, without sources. The comparison of Israel and Judah to liberals and conservatives is the pastor’s own illustration. Three spots are marked [unclear]: the first words of the sentence about a child maturing, the last word of “a glorious [unclear],” and the last phrase of the closing (“we’re togethering into” in the captions).

chunks.section_question: What does God promise in the midst of judgment?
chunks.short_answer: He says he will look at “precious promises before, during, and after Sodom’s judgment,” and that in the midst of war, famine and captivity God has another message for people who will listen to the message of repentance. He says Jeremiah spoke shortly before the captivity while nations warred around Judah and false prophets said nothing would happen, and asks, “Does it sound like America today?”
chunks.text:
We’re going to take a look at precious promises before, during, and after Sodom’s judgment that God pronounced on the wicked, on the wicked believers and people that would reject the message of repentance. Okay? Now remember in the midst of these messages that we preached previously, the judgments, the war, the famines, the acts of God, the captivity where they lost their home, their family members, they lost their nation, they were taken away from their nation, everything that they knew. In the midst of these judgments, there’s another message that God has for the people that will listen to the message of repentance.

Okay? And Jeremiah is speaking less than 20 year or less than 30 years before the captivity is going to happen. He is speaking 11 years. The Egyptian war, the Egyptian nation and the Assyrian nation and the Babylonian nation are warring, and Judah is right in the middle of it. And it’s happening all around them. And Jeremiah’s preaching what’s going to— the, these guys. Israel has already been carried away captive and destroyed by war and famine. And now we find Judah still even though all these things are going on around about them.

chunks.section_question: Is God still married to His people? (Jeremiah 3:14, 2 Corinthians 11:2)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Jeremiah 3:14, “Return, repent, oh backsliding children, says the Lord, for I am married to you,” and says God hates divorce, so He is not wanting to divorce us. He says this applies to the church as well as Judah, citing 2 Corinthians 11:2, and that “Yes, he will punish us. Yes, he will correct us,” but He is married to us.
chunks.text:
They think and they believe and they speak. Their false prophets speak that nothing’s going to happen to Judah. Does it sound like America today? All these wars, all this sin going on in their nation, all this trouble around us. A lot of the nations I’ve preached in a lot of the nations in the world and they hate America. You know, America just don’t get it. Are you there? And in the midst of this, God comes with the other side of the message. Jeremiah 3:14: “Return, repent, oh backsliding children, says the Lord, for I am married to you.” Now, the Bible says that God hates what? Divorce. And he’s married to us. So, is he wanting to divorce us?

Are you out there? See, this is pertinent stuff. It’s important. See, he is God was married to his Jews, his Jewish people back there. He’s married to his church. And he reminds even though he’s telling them all these judgments are coming, he reminds them that you’re my bride. You’re married to me. And so not only for that group back in Judah at that time, but also for the church. Jeremiah is prophesying. In 2 Corinthians 11:2: “I’ve espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” Amen. So who is the wife of Christ? The church. Yes. You see, he’s married to us. Yes, he will punish us. Yes, he will correct us.

chunks.section_question: Is Christ coming back for a mature bride? (Revelation 19:7, Revelation 21:9)
chunks.short_answer: He says God is not giving up on us “because we got some problems,” and cites Revelation 19:7 and 21:9, saying Christ will return for a mature, righteous bride, not “a baby church.” He says most end-time preachers bring only the seven years of tribulation and the antichrist, which he says “isn’t even in there,” and he gives David reclaiming his bride from another man as an illustration of Jesus taking us from Satan.
chunks.text:
But he’s married to us and he isn’t giving up on us because we got some problems. Amen. He’s just asking us to change our stupid ways. In Revelation 19:7, “the marriage of the Lamb has come and his wife has made herself ready.” Speaking of the second return of Christ, the church will be a mature, righteous dressed in white linen bride when Christ comes. And this is what most of the end time prophetic preachers aren’t bringing in. All they bring in is the seven years of tribulation and the antichrist, which isn’t even in there. You have to twist scriptures to get that out. One man being an antichrist and son of perdition and all that. But when Christ comes back, is he coming back for a baby church or a mature bride church?

Yeah. Do men marry children? No. [unclear] that child has to grow up and mature and take on that shape that these women have to get these men’s attention. And in the spiritual, that’s exactly what’s going to happen. Jesus is going to build a glorious church. And he’s coming back for that glorious [unclear]. Also in Revelation 21:9: “I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” And he showed Jerusalem coming down out of the heaven as a bride prepared for her husband. Okay. Now again in Jeremiah 3:14-18: “I will take you from one city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.”

He said, “I’m married to you, and I’m going to go and get my bride.” Now, King David is an illustration of this. King David’s first wife was taken by her father. David had to go into the wilderness. Her father married her off to another man. And when King David got through his wilderness wanderings and God’s promise came to him and he was made king, he went and got his bride back from that husband that wasn’t his her real husband. You see, when we’re in sin, when we’re in the kingdom of darkness, we’re married to Satan. We have a relationship with Satan. But Jesus comes by his blood and the power of his resurrection and he takes us from that bad husband and he brings us unto himself.

chunks.short_answer: He quotes “I will give you shepherds according to my heart who will feed you with knowledge and understanding,” and says we need knowledge and understanding. He cites Jesus as the good shepherd and Hebrews, that God now speaks to us through His Son.
chunks.text: Now, what is these pastors that God is sending doing? Feeding us with what? Knowledge and understanding. Hallelujah. How many of you know that’s what we need? We need some knowledge and understanding. And the scriptures back it up. Number one, in John 10:1, Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd.” “I am the good shepherd.” Folks, in Hebrews it says God spoke in the old days to our forefathers by the prophets, but now he speaks to us through his son Jesus Christ. chunks.section_question: Why isn’t zeal without knowledge enough? (Romans 10:2-3)
chunks.short_answer: He says “no undershepherd has the right to give you their opinion,” only the truth from the Bible. He cites Romans 10:2–3, “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge,” and says some Christians are stirred up for Jesus but don’t go to Sunday school or Bible studies or open their Bible through the week.
chunks.text:
Even though Jeremiah said, “I will send you shepherds plural,” no undershepherd has the right to teach anything but what the shepherd Jesus said to teach. No undershepherd has the right to give you their opinion. They must give you the truth from the Bible. Period. In Romans 10:2: “They have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.” Here the Jews, he’s talking about the Jews. Yeah, they have a zeal of God. They’re stirred up for God, but they don’t have the knowledge. How many of you know Christians like that? You know, they’re stirred up for Jesus and they don’t even know him. Why? They have no knowledge. They don’t go to Sunday school. They don’t go to Bible studies where the word is being taught and they don’t open their book through the week. Got no time to study the Bible.

Got time for everything, but can’t study the Bible, which is our new covenant promise that he would inscribe it in our minds and our hearts. But how can he inscribe when we’re not hearing it, listening to it, reading it, and studying it? Can I hear an amen? Amen. Also in Romans 10:3: “Being ignorant of God’s righteousness and going about to establish their own righteousness.” See, they don’t have the knowledge of God’s righteousness. And the Bible tells us in first John that “he that doeth righteous is righteous.” Duh. Amen. And so they’re ignorant of what God says is right. Jeremiah 4:22 says, “My people are foolish.

chunks.section_question: What are God’s people destroyed for lack of? (Hosea 4:6)

He cites Hosea 4:6, “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge,” and says it does not say lack of faith, grace, or the baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues. He then reads that in the midst of warnings, “Jerusalem shall be called the throne of the Lord.”
chunks.text:
They haven’t known me. They are stubborn children. They have no understanding. They are wise to do evil, but to do good, they have no knowledge.” And this is the American church. We talk about Jesus. We talk about the Bible, but we don’t know him. And we do evil because we don’t bother finding out what God says is right and what God says is wrong and avoid the wrong and do right. Can I hear an amen? In Hosea 4:6, “My people are destroyed for lack of faith.” No, you guys shaking your head. That’s right. It doesn’t say that. “My people are destroyed for lack of grace.” No, it doesn’t say that either. “My people are destroyed for the lack of the baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues and prophecy.”

chunks.section_question: Does God promise increase in the midst of judgment?
chunks.short_answer: He says that in the middle of a message of famine, war and captivity, God says, “I’m going to increase you,” a message to the righteous alongside the message to the wicked. He says there were 7,000 who never bowed to Baal, and people like Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, Ezekiel, Jeremiah, Ezra and Esther who listened and were multiplied.
chunks.text: Here he comes and says, “Hey, I’m going to increase you.” Totally the opposite of the other side of the prophecy. Are you hearing me? So, in the midst of the message to the wicked, he has a message to the righteous. In spite of these things coming, in spite of the wicked, continue to do wickedly. Believers that do wickedly, unbelievers that do wickedly, I’m going to increase you and I’m going to multiply you. And we found that he did. In Israel, there were 7,000 that never bowed their knee to Baal, nor kissed his feet. There were people in the northern kingdom that served God. We know there were people in the southern kingdom that came to God at this time. Daniel was one of them. Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, Ezekiel, Jeremiah here.

He says home Bible studies have the same problems as denominations, and “we need to get rid of these problems and get back to the book.”
chunks.text:

And Jeremiah is also speaking to the church that is a far off several hundred years when Christ comes. Okay. Now, how does that relate to us today? If we confess our sins, he’s what? Faithful and just to forgive us our sins. What do you think you’re going to be doing when you stand before the judgment throne? Defending your choices? No. You’re going to be admitting, confessing you were wrong. Wouldn’t it be better to do that now? Amen. You say, “I’m wrong, Lord.” Jesus is the one we’re [unclear] into. Jesus is the one that can deliver us. Jesus is the one that can save America. Jesus is the one that can change my life today.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For all people walk each in the name of his god, But we will walk in the name of the LORD our God Forever and ever.
that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth,
For it is written: “As I live, says the LORD, Every knee shall bow to Me, And every tongue shall confess to God.”
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

faqs.question: When does he say Jeremiah was speaking?
faqs.answer: He says Jeremiah spoke less than 30 years before the captivity, with the Egyptian, Assyrian and Babylonian nations at war around Judah, and Israel already carried away captive.

faqs.question: What does he say the false prophets told Judah?
faqs.answer: He says they spoke that “nothing’s going to happen to Judah,” even with wars and sin all around. He asks whether that sounds like America today.

faqs.question: Who does he say is the wife of Christ?
faqs.answer: He says “The church,” citing 2 Corinthians 11:2, and that God reminds even a disciplined people, “you’re my bride.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

faqs.question: Is Christ coming back for a baby church?
faqs.answer: He asks, “is he coming back for a baby church or a mature bride church?” He says the church will be a mature, righteous bride dressed in white linen when Christ comes.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.”

faqs.question: What is his illustration from King David?
faqs.answer: He says David’s first wife was married off to another man by her father, and after David became king he went and got his bride back. He says Jesus likewise takes us from the “bad husband” by His blood and the power of His resurrection.

faqs.question: Why does he say some Christians lack knowledge?
faqs.answer: He says some don’t go to Sunday school or Bible studies “and they don’t open their book through the week.” He says they have time for everything but studying the Bible.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

faqs.question: How does he say God writes His word in us?
faqs.answer: He says it is the new covenant promise that God would inscribe it in our minds and hearts, but asks “how can he inscribe when we’re not hearing it, listening to it, reading it, and studying it?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put My laws in their mind and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.

faqs.question: Does he say young people who fall away come back?
faqs.answer: He says 50% of those who fell away come back “like the prodigal in the pig pen,” which “puts the percentages in our favor.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by “Gentile”?
faqs.answer: He says Gentile is someone who doesn’t believe in God the Creator or in Jesus. He says the word nation in your Bible is almost every time Gentile: “It’s those that don’t believe in God.”

faqs.question: Must we preach both the bad news and the good news?
faqs.answer: He says “If you’re going to preach the bad news, you got to preach the good news. If you’re going to preach the good news, you got to preach the bad news.” He says, “It’s got to be balanced.”

faqs.question: What does he say we will be doing at the judgment throne?
faqs.answer: He says we will not be defending our choices: “You’re going to be admitting, confessing you were wrong.” He says it would be better to do that now.

scriptures.text_nkjv: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
